Game Name (working title)
LAST ROUTE
"No one knows why the road is still open."
Core Idea
You and up to 5 friends are driving one truck across a frozen mountain to deliver the last generator core to a dying town.
Without it...
Thousands of people freeze.
So turning back isn't an option.
Core Gameplay Loop
Drive ⬇ Reach checkpoint ⬇ Random event ⬇ Solve it together ⬇ Repair truck ⬇ Continue ⬇ Repeat ⬇ Final escape
The truck almost never stops for long. The journey is the game.
The BIG Hook
The Storm Changes Every Run.
Not just weather.
The storm changes the world.
Examples:
🌨 Heavy snow.
Visibility 5 metres.
🧊 Frozen lake.
Road disappears.
Drive over ice.
Risk breaking through.
🌲 Fallen trees.
Need axes.
⛰ Avalanche.
New road opens.
Old road closes.
📡 Strange radio signal.
Follow it...
Or ignore it.
🏚 Abandoned village appears.
Sometimes.
Not every run.
Every run feels different.
Player Jobs
Everyone naturally gets a role.
🚛 Driver
Can only focus on driving.
🗺 Navigator
Uses map.
Finds routes.
Reads signs.
🔧 Mechanic
Repairs truck.
Keeps engine alive.
Changes tyres.
📦 Scavenger
Searches buildings.
Gets fuel.
Food.
Medicine.
Parts.
🔦 Lookout
Uses binoculars.
Warns about danger.
Nobody is standing around.
The Horror
No zombie waves.
No screaming monster.
Something...
Is following the truck.
It never attacks directly.
Instead...
Fuel disappears.
Doors open.
Lights go out.
Tyre tracks appear beside yours.
Someone knocks...
But nobody is there.
The mystery is the horror.
Mid Game Twist
You discover...
Every abandoned truck looks exactly like yours.
Same number.
Same cargo.
Same scratches.
How?
Nobody knows.
Now players start theorising.
Final Act
The storm gets insane.
Truck barely works.
Visibility almost zero.
Radio cuts in.
Someone says...
"Don't let it overtake you."
Now everyone panics.
You don't even know what "it" is.
Ending
Reach the town.
Unload generator.
Lights come on.
Storm instantly stops.
Outside...
Your truck has six sets of footprints around it.
Nobody says anything.
Game ends.
Players immediately start discussing what happened.
Why I think this is stronger
The mystery is what people remember.
Not:
"Big monster killed me."
But:
"WHY WAS THERE ANOTHER TRUCK?"
Those kinds of mysteries create YouTube theory videos.
MVP (cheap version)
One truck.
One mountain road.
Three checkpoints.
10-15 random events.
One ending.
No giant open world.
No massive AI.
The game could be finished in about 20-30 minutes per run.
But here's the one thing I'd still change.
I wouldn't make it a pure horror game.
I'd make it 70% adventure, 30% horror.
If players are scared the whole time, the fear wears off. If most of the game is about teamwork, driving, and making decisions, then the strange moments hit much harder because they're unexpected.
One last thing: if your goal is a viral Roblox game, don't try to beat Dead Rails by adding more monsters or more mechanics. Beat it by making players ask one question after every run:
"Wait... what actually happened out there?"
That kind of mystery gives people a reason to replay, tell their friends, and watch theory videos. That's much harder to copy than just another survival game.

answers.ask: A mountain road with three checkpoints is a long strip - should it be one region-scale map, or three chapter maps joined at the checkpoints?
answers.answer: Use one compact region-scale mountain road with all three checkpoints along it. The MVP is one road and the journey should feel continuous, not split into separate chapter maps.

answers.ask: Should the abandoned village be a fixed location on the route, or does it need to be omittable since it only appears on some runs?
answers.answer: Make it omittable: it appears only on some runs as a random route-side event/location. It should not be a fixed required stop.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] scale — Q: A mountain road with three checkpoints is a long strip - should it be one region-scale map, or three chapter maps joined at the checkpoints? A: Use one compact region-scale mountain road with all three checkpoints along it. The MVP is one road and the journey should feel continuous, not split into separate chapter maps.
- [author] shape — Q: Should the abandoned village be a fixed location on the route, or does it need to be omittable since it only appears on some runs? A: Make it omittable: it appears only on some runs as a random route-side event/location. It should not be a fixed required stop.
- [agent_inferred] event layout — Q: How should changing road events fit one continuous route? A: Use event sockets and short alternate branches along a permanently connected start-to-town route.

## Enriched image prompt
Build one continuous compact region-scale frozen mountain route for a six-person truck journey. A single snowbound road begins at a truck staging point, passes exactly three checkpoints, and ends at a cold dark town where a generator core is unloaded. Wind the road across tiered mountain terrain and add 10–15 modular event sockets with short alternate branches. These sockets can interchange near-zero-visibility snow, a frozen-lake crossing, fallen-tree blockages, an avalanche opening or closing a road, a strange radio beacon, repeated abandoned trucks, or an optional abandoned village without making every event appear in one run. Include enterable roadside structures for scavenging, while keeping the final town visible as the journey’s distant orientation landmark. Preserve one continuous driveable point-to-point route in the elevated composition.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Adventure (`adventure`), matching the author’s stated 70% journey focus, with Survival (`survival`) secondary for environmental danger and scavenging.

## Shape and preset
Use `route-point-to-point` from outside Adventure’s usual set: one driveable course starts at the truck staging point and terminates at the town. Use the Guided Trail preset with this substituted shape and without `reveal-exit`; the route and destination landmark remain its recognisable core.

## Config requirements
Use `path-trail` for the single frozen mountain road, `landmark-focal` for the destination town, `terrain-relief` for the mountain slopes, and `building-interior` for scavengable roadside structures. Use `chunk-modular`, taken from the shared catalogue, for the 10–15 interchangeable event sections. Within those modules, use `hazard-kill` for avalanche or breakable-ice danger and `water-body` for the optional frozen-lake crossing. One truck and the omittable village are scene-specific geometry.

## Layout requirements
Place exactly three `checkpoint-respawn` markers at road stops in route order. Use `collectible-nodes` for fuel, food, medicine, and repair parts inside roadside buildings and near abandoned vehicles. Place 10–15 free-text TriggerZone event sockets, including one capable of loading or omitting the village. Place one free-text TriggerZone completion marker in the final town’s generator-unloading area.

## Layout components
The map contains one start, one truck, one continuous mountain road, exactly three checkpoints, short alternate branches, 10–15 event sockets, roadside interiors, optional frozen-lake, avalanche, and village modules, repeated abandoned-truck sites, and one destination town. Mountain barriers enclose the corridor, and the road remains connected from start to finish in every event combination.

## Render order
Use `authored_plan`: generate the supported `route-point-to-point` road, checkpoints, alternates, and event sockets as the authoritative blueprint before producing top-down and isometric images.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is large, compressing the compact region enough to keep the truck, checkpoints, road, and structures legible over a 20–30 minute route. The theme is realistic frozen-mountain adventure with restrained mystery horror. Use `P6` for route and modular-section validity, `tiered` for mountain relief, `P3` for roadside interiors, and `CHECK` for the optional frozen-lake play envelope.

Tiered frozen mountain slopes and relief that the road winds across.
Enterable roadside structures for scavenging along the route.
10–15 modular event sockets with short alternate branches that swap in different road events without breaking the continuous route.
Optional danger modules such as an avalanche opening/closing the road or breakable ice hazards within event sections.
An optional frozen-lake crossing module as one of the interchangeable event sections.

Fuel, food, medicine, and repair parts placed inside roadside buildings and near abandoned vehicles.

notes: Preset recorded as 'Guided Trail' exactly as named in the blob, even though the shape was substituted to `route-point-to-point` and `reveal-exit` was excluded per blob.
Blob specifies 10–15 event sockets; schema has no canonical option for free-text TriggerZone sockets, so they are captured under layout.props rather than options/layout_placement.
Blob specifies a free-text TriggerZone completion marker; captured under layout.props for the same reason.
No explicit frame-relative placement rules ('where') were given for some non-layout props beyond general locations; recorded verbatim where possible without inventing additional siting detail.
